**A Dynamic Island for your Android punch-hole — running over every app on the phone.**

Not a mock-up and not a wallpaper: a system overlay that turns your camera cutout into a live pill showing what is actually playing, ringing and charging.

This is the biggest release so far. The control panel used to be one long scroll that did everything; it is now **three tabs**, and the island itself is finally something you can shape rather than just switch on.

## Download

| File | Install this? | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **`dcp-v2.6.0-release.apk`** | **Yes** | 172,023 bytes |
| `dcp-v2.6.0-debug.apk` | Only if you're attaching a debugger | 238,413 bytes |

The debug build installs *alongside* the release one as `com.dcp.punch.debug`, labelled **DCP (debug)** — they no longer collide.

**Check your download before installing.** A phone browser that lands on a GitHub *page* instead of the file will save an HTML error page under the `.apk` name, and the installer then calls the APK corrupt. The size column above is the quickest tell — a few KB means you got a web page. To be certain:

```
sha256  release  9e5a573ced2f4dc4cb729e4aa9d65fbb72c4d415f7a6749648591a01bec9c5cb
sha256  debug    a8e7aebcbcce7c4765c00f304a95040277933be957997951e7ff906a5ea9efc7
```

Both are signed with APK Signature Scheme v2 and verify with `apksigner verify` across the whole supported range, API 24 to 34.

## What's new in 2.6.0

### Three tabs

| Tab | What lives there |
|---|---|
| **Cards** | Everything the island *shows* — the two allow-lists with their **+** pickers, the notification-content switches, "show only on the island", and the new gesture assignments. |
| **Look** | Everything about how it *looks and moves*, with a live preview at the top. |
| **Settings** | Your name, the theme switches, the device readout, the support page, and the setup checklist. |

A sliding pill tracks the active tab, panes cross-fade and rise 14dp, and tabs dip 6% under a finger — so a tap is acknowledged before the pane has finished arriving.

### Look — seventeen dials over a live preview

Position on both axes · compact corner radius · expanded radius · expanded width · idle scale · opacity at rest · border width · background colour · outline colour · shadow strength · animation speed · bounce · reduce animation · glow · arrive-expanded · auto-hide seconds — plus the cutout shape.

Above them, a **live preview** loops idle → compact → expanded using your current settings, so a dial's effect is visible without leaving the screen. Each slider fires cheap updates while you drag and commits on release, so fiddling with the look doesn't thrash the live overlay redrawing behind the app. The preview stops the moment its window is invisible — an animation nobody can see is pure battery.

### Presets, with your own names

Save the whole Look tab as "Night", "Discreet", "Big and loud" — whatever you like — and switch between them in one tap. Saving over a name replaces it instead of stacking a second copy. Stored as JSON, so a dial added in a later version needs no migration: an unknown key is ignored and a missing one falls back to its default.

### Gestures you assign yourself

Five gestures — **tap, double tap, long press, swipe left, swipe right** — each settable to: open the app, expand, collapse, dismiss, swap, play/pause, next track, previous track, or nothing.

Double tap defaults to **nothing** on purpose: with nothing bound to it, a single tap fires the instant you lift your finger instead of waiting 300 ms to find out whether a second one is coming. Bind it and taps get that delay back — worth knowing before you do.

Assignments are stored **by name, not by position in a menu**, so inserting a new action in a later version can't silently remap "open the app" to "play/pause". That's the kind of bug nobody thinks to look for.

### CPU and storage, next to RAM

The Settings tab now reports all three: total/available/used **RAM**, used and free **storage**, and the **chipset** with its core count.

The CPU figure is **this app's own share of wall-clock time**, and the card says so. A live system-wide CPU percentage has not been readable by an ordinary Android app since `/proc/stat` was restricted in Android 8 — precisely so apps couldn't fingerprint the device that way. Any app showing you a system CPU meter without root is a system app or is making it up. This shows the number it can genuinely measure, labelled as its own.

### A support page, bundled and offline

Opened from Settings, running in the `:demo` process so it costs nothing while closed. It makes **no network requests at all** — the web font became a system stack and the remote image a local one — which is the only version that could work anyway in an app that declares no `INTERNET` permission. Nine browser assertions check it, starting with "issues zero requests".

> ⚠️ **The page ships without a QR image.** `donate-qr.png` wasn't supplied and one was deliberately not generated — an invented payment QR could route a real payment to the wrong place. There's a labelled placeholder, and the account details on the page are copyable as they are. Drop your own PNG at `android/app/src/main/assets/support/donate-qr.png` and rebuild to add it.

### On Material Capsule

None of its code, assets, layouts or strings were copied. The features were reimplemented from scratch — which is also the only way they fit a build with **no libraries in it at all**: no AndroidX, no Kotlin runtime, no third-party code. That's why a system-wide overlay, a three-tab control panel, a support page and the full web demo all fit in 168 KB.

---

## RAM

Working set is still **30–45 MB**, and everything new was built to stay out of the way: the preview stops when it isn't visible, sliders write only on release, the three panes are inflated once and cross-faded rather than rebuilt, and the support page lives in the `:demo` process so closing it hands every byte back to the system instead of leaving a fattened heap inside the process that hosts your overlay.

## Permissions

Still exactly **six**, every one read by code in this app. No `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` — the app picker uses a `<queries>` declaration, which sees only apps with a launcher icon. **No `INTERNET`** — this app has never made a network request and cannot.

## Setup

1. **Display over other apps** — required. This is the permission that lets the island draw on top of everything.
2. **Notification access** — optional but recommended; this is what makes the content real rather than just charging and ringer events.
3. **Show notifications** — Android requires an ongoing notification for a service that runs indefinitely. That notice is also how you turn the theme off.

Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24) · targetSdk 34 · ~168 KB on disk.

## Verified before release

- `clean assembleRelease assembleDebug lintDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL, zero lint errors**
- Both APKs `apksigner verify` → **VERIFIED**, API 24 through 34
- Permission list: exactly six, no `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, no `INTERNET`
- Web demo: **31 browser assertions**, including all 23 presentations driven through compact *and* expanded in both cutout shapes, each measured for clipped text, plus both edge-swipe directions
- Support page: **9 assertions**, the first being "issues zero requests"

## Not verified

**The APK has never been launched on a phone.** The build machine has no KVM, so no emulator can boot on it — everything above is structural and static verification. The first install is the real smoke test. If something breaks on your device, that's a genuine finding, not a known issue being glossed over.
